memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him to consecrate him." - Lev 8:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Not a dab. Not a smear. Poured.

David later described this moment in a psalm about unity: It is like precious oil poured on the head, running down on the beard, running down on Aaron's beard, down on the collar of his robe (Ps 133:2). The picture is of abundance — oil overflowing, going everywhere, impossible to contain.

Oil throughout Scripture is associated with God's Spirit and His setting apart of a person for service. Kings were anointed. Prophets were anointed. Priests were anointed.

And the Hebrew word for "anointed one" is mashiach — Messiah. In Greek, Christos. Christ.

Every anointing in the Old Testament was a small rehearsal for the One who would be Prophet, Priest, and King together. Jesus stood in the synagogue at Nazareth, read from Isaiah — The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me — and said, Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing (Lk 4:18-21).

And John writes to ordinary believers: You have an anointing from the Holy One (1 Jn 2:20).

The oil poured on Aaron's head has, in Christ, reached you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live conscious that God's Spirit has been given to me?
2. What has God set me apart for that I have been treating as ordinary?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the Spirit You have poured out through Christ. Fill me afresh and use me for the purposes You have set me apart for. Amen.
